Simulate and Evaluate the Composition Prototype

operations.Rd

Use a compatibility bridge, or assemble a numeric FRPP likelihood from public emhawkes kernel replay output and the residual law.

Usage

fsim(object, size = 100, lambda_component0 = "auto", N0 = NULL,
    Nc0 = NULL, seed = NULL, ...)
# S3 method for class 'fspec'
simulate(object, nsim = 1, seed = NULL, size = 100,
    lambda_component0 = "auto", N0 = NULL, Nc0 = NULL, ...)
# S3 method for class 'fspec'
logLik(object, inter_arrival, type = NULL, mark = NULL,
    N = NULL, Nc = NULL, N0 = NULL, Nc0 = NULL,
    lambda_component0 = "auto", infer = FALSE,
    backend = c("bridge", "state"), ...)

Arguments

object

An fspec. Old frpp_spec objects are also supported.

nsim

One path is supported. Use size for its length.

seed

Optional seed. When supplied, the caller's RNG state is restored.

size

Number of output rows including the initial row.

lambda_component0

Initial kernel components. Automatic initialization uses zero for the residual-distribution model. Supply an explicit state when known. A Hawkes stationary mean is not automatically applied to FRPP.

N0, Nc0

Initial counts and mark totals, passed to emhawkes.

inter_arrival, type, mark

Observations starting with an initial zero row.

N, Nc

Optional observed count paths.

infer

Return driver states, likelihood and residual diagnostics.

backend

bridge delegates to the existing FRPP likelihood. state independently assembles the residual likelihood from the kernel's public replay output. This requires the emhawkes development kernel API; with earlier versions, use bridge.

...

Additional public emhawkes arguments for the bridge. The state prototype accepts none.

Details

Simulation retains the existing R FRPP loop and requires equal decay rates within each row. Every global event refreshes all candidate residuals. The state backend currently supports numeric kernels, numeric mark effects and kernel mappings, with equal decay rates within each row and no impact or mark-density callbacks. Callback specifications remain available through the bridge. Kernel states and their integrals are drivers; with a non-exponential residual law they are not automatically the FRPP conditional intensities.

For event type j in a global inter-event interval, its contribution is $$\log v_j + \log f(A_j) + \sum_{k \ne j}\log S(A_k),$$ where v is the pre-event kernel driver and A is its interval integral. The public replay call returns kernel-only interval integrals and pre-event sums. The FRPP layer adds baseline contributions. Full component histories are retained only with infer = TRUE; interval integrals and sums use memory proportional to path length times the number of event types. This backend does not evaluate a Hawkes likelihood. fsim() is the primary simulation function; the simulate() methods call it and return the same path.

The existing emhawkes.engine option retains its original meaning. In particular, the bridge does not support a forced C++ FRPP likelihood.

Value

Simulation returns a frpp_path list containing its composition model and the original path fields other than the transitional hspec field. Likelihood evaluation returns the existing named numeric value, or an inference list. The state backend additionally returns integrated_driver. No fitted degrees of freedom or confidence intervals are supplied.

Examples

kernel <- methods::new("hspec", mu = .3, alpha = .2, beta = 1)
model <- fspec(kernel, residual_law(c(shape = 2, rate = 2),
    stats::dgamma, stats::pgamma, stats::qgamma, stats::rgamma))
path <- fsim(model, size = 12, seed = 73, lambda_component0 = 0)
stats::logLik(model, path$inter_arrival, path$type, lambda_component0 = 0)
#> loglikelihood 
#>     -22.68649 
if ("exp_kernel_replay" %in% getNamespaceExports("emhawkes")) {
  stats::logLik(model, path$inter_arrival, path$type, lambda_component0 = 0,
                backend = "state")
}
